newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down on speculative dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down on speculative dlr buying.

text.p: The won closed lower on Tuesday as speculative U.S. dollar buyers outweighed an earlier round of U.S. dollar profit-taking in the local market, dealers said.

"Speculation on the dollar's continued strength prompted position build-ups. But Profit-taking emerged due to the dollar's slide against the yen," said Ha Jong-soo, a dealer with the Korea Exchange Bank (KEB).
The won ended at 828.80 after opening at 827.20. It ranged from 826.80 and 829.10.
Dealers said they expected the dollar would rise further on Wednesday on dollar demand from importers.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 828.50 on Wednesday, compared with 827.70 today.
Ha of the KEB forecast trading would move between 827.00 and 830.00 on Wednesday, while a Korea Development Bank dealer put it between 828.00 and 830.00.
